findings.comment: Synchronizing Browser configuration attributes inside Agent.__init__ mutates an injected browser instance's context config (even if a custom browser_context was already provided, or if new_context_config was explicitly configured). Additionally, this synchronization will not take effect when Browser is used independently of Agent.

Hardcoding channel='chrome' causes two issues: 1) It will raise a runtime error when self.config.browser_class is 'firefox' or 'webkit' because neither supports the 'chrome' channel. 2) Unlike bundled Chromium installed via 'playwright install chromium', channel='chrome' requires a system installation of Google Chrome and will fail if Chrome is not installed in the environment (such as in Docker or CI).

When self.browser.config.headless is False, neither viewport nor no_viewport is added to kwargs. Previously, no_viewport=True was passed unconditionally. In headed mode, Playwright/Patchright falls back to its default viewport (1280x720), ignoring self.config.browser_window_size (1280x1100) and preventing the viewport from matching the browser window. In addition, the existing self.config.no_viewport attribute is never respected.

All imports across the codebase have been migrated from `playwright` to `patchright`. Since `patchright` serves as a drop-in replacement, retaining `playwright>=1.51.0` in `dependencies` appears redundant and will cause both packages to be installed.
